# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, `reading_mark`, `reading_grow_dst`, `reading_newStack`, all by `decide` on
library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. No verdict changes on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft].

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack gives `reject`. Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in
`d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

**DS-R9 `newStack` preconditions: §76.5 applies [draft]** (was R5; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says nothing about creation. Reading: those of `newArena` other than its guard
(`Arena.NewArenaBase`: §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 "All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are
already `Init`", read for a stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)` (§56). Alternative: drop
§76.5 for a stack (DS-v1 does not take over `newArena`). Same choice as H-R8 for pools. Example
(`Witness.reading_newStack`, decided on the initial state of statics `wsu`): leaf 0, `Uninit`, owns
the storage leaf 1 and so holds its root authority 1 (§47); `newStack(1, 1)` is `reject` (only
§76.5 fails: every other field of `NewArenaBase` and the guard hold), `ok` under the alternative.

**DS-R10 `mark` requires no right [draft]** (was R6; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1 says nothing about
a right for `mark`. Reading: `ok` on an existing stack, `reject` on a missing one; `mark` changes
library metadata only and creates no right (§36 ¶2, §38). Alternative: §36 ¶1, metadata is modified
"to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts", so `mark` needs a right on the
stack value (`AdminRight`, or a valid `writeShared` over it, §68), else `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_mark`): in `d13` (a callee frame entered after the rewind), the callee has no
`AdminRight`, no `Observe` right on the stack value 0 and no valid `writeShared` over it through any
authority; `mark(0)` is `ok` (a mark appended), `reject` under the alternative.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. Under the stack invariants (internal a `Modify` authority held by
  the stack value whose footprint contains the cells) and I3, `ok` holds exactly when DS-v1's
  condition and §36 hold; this converse is **not proved** here.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5, R6, R7:** moved to DS-R9, DS-R10, DS-R11 above (they change verdicts or arrival states;
  review round 2, DS-1).
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.

**DS-R11 `grow` destination: the recorded `Blk.dst` [draft]** (was R7; review round 2, DS-1). DS-v1
says only "grow is in place only" and "uses the derived issue"; it does not name the destination.
Reading: the destination recorded for the block at `push` (`Blk.dst`), even when the block value has
been transferred since and that place is `Moved`. Alternative: the place that currently holds `b`.
Changes the arrival state. Example (`Witness.reading_grow_dst`): after the first push (block 5
stored at place 4), the program's `transfer(4, 5)` (§63) moves authority 5 to place 5 and makes
place 4 `Moved` (`d14`). `grow(0, 5, 1)` is `ok` and stores the new block authority 6 into place 4,
which becomes `Init` (§65), while place 5 keeps the released authority 5 (`d15`). Under the
alternative, the static checks of the derived issue (`IssueStatic`) and `store(6, 5)` are `ok` on
the same released and split state, and authority 6 is held by place 5.

Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).

Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.
3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.
7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Each case: reached state from the initial state, expected verdict from its source, positive twin for each rejection, class. MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass. Docstrings: model modules: every def/theorem cites the specification clause it formalizes. Library modules: cite the applicable spec clauses (§36, §56, ...) and the local contract identifier (HandlePool v0.4 annex, DS-v1), stated as non-normative.
Exclusions: instrumented checked variants; duplicate _pre statements; references to draft reports; concurrency beyond the stat boundary; syntax.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

95	  | .writeShared a ls => WriteSharedStep k a ls s
96	  | .pin p => PinStep p s
97	  | .unpin p => UnpinStep k p s
98	  | .endUse p => EndUseStep k p s
99	  | .free p auth => FreeStep k p auth s
100	  | .alloc pr ow ls => AllocStep k pr ow ls s
101	  | .store a p => StoreStep a p s
102	  | .newArena .. | .issue .. | .reset .. => fun _ => False
103	
104	/-- The relation of a stack-library operation from `D` (DS-v1, non-normative; §58): the kernel
105	relation of O1–O16 with the stack metadata unchanged; `NewStackStep` with no other registry
106	(§56: the library states of these runs hold stacks only), `PushStep`, `MarkStep`, `RewindStep`,
107	`GrowStep`. -/
108	def DOpRel (k : K) (D : DState) : DOp → Outcome3 DState → Prop
109	  | .kernel o _ => KRelD (kRel k D.kern o) D
110	  | .newStack st i => NewStackStep [] st i D
111	  | .push j size dst => PushStep k j size dst D
112	  | .mark j => MarkStep j D
113	  | .rewind j m => RewindStep k j m D
114	  | .grow j b extra => GrowStep k j b extra D
115	
116	section Exec
117	variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
118	  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
119	  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
120	
121	/-- A kernel outcome computed by the corpus runner, read on stack-library states (§58; DS-v1):
122	the stack metadata unchanged on `ok`. -/
123	def liftK (D : DState) : Outcome3 LState → Outcome3 DState
124	  | .ok L => .ok ⟨L.kern, D.stacks, D.fresh⟩
125	  | .reject => .reject
126	  | .fail => .fail
127	
128	/-- The computed outcome of a stack-library operation from `D` (DS-v1, non-normative; §58): the
129	kernel operations by the corpus runner on the kernel state; the stack operations by the order of
130	the checks of their relations. -/
131	def dstep (D : DState) : DOp → Outcome3 DState
132	  | .kernel o _ => liftK D (lstep k ⟨D.kern, []⟩ o)
133	  | .newStack st i =>
134	    if NewStackPre D.kern D.stacks [] st i then .ok (newStackEff D st i) else .reject
135	  | .push j size dst =>
136	    match D.stacks[j]? with
137	    | none => .reject
138	    | some st =>
139	      if IssueStatic D.kern st.entry (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
140	        if st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length then
141	          if SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size] then
142	            if StorePre (splitEff D.kern st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size]) D.kern.A.length
143	                dst then
144	              .ok ⟨storeEff (splitEff D.kern st.internal [cellsOf st st.top size])
145	                  D.kern.A.length dst,
146	                D.stacks.set j (pushMeta st size D.kern.A.length dst), D.fresh⟩
147	            else .reject
148	          else .reject
149	        else .fail
150	      else .reject
151	  | .mark j =>
152	    match D.stacks[j]? with
153	    | none => .reject
154	    | some st => .ok ⟨D.kern, D.stacks.set j (markMeta j st D.fresh), D.fresh + 1⟩
155	  | .rewind j m =>
156	    match D.stacks[j]? with
157	    | none => .reject
158	    | some st =>
159	      if LiveMark j st m then
160	        if AdminRight D.kern st then
161	          if SplitPre k D.kern st.internal [above st m] then
162	            if ReleasePre (splitEff D.kern st.internal [above st m]) D.kern.A.length then
163	              .ok ⟨releaseEff (splitEff D.kern st.internal [above st m]) D.kern.A.length,
164	                D.stacks.set j (rewindMeta st m), D.fresh⟩
165	            else .reject
166	          else .reject
167	        else .reject
168	      else .fail
169	  | .grow j b extra =>
170	    match D.stacks[j]? with
171	    | none => .reject
172	    | some st =>
173	      match st.block b with
174	      | none => .reject
175	      | some x =>
176	        if 0 < extra then
177	          if ReleasePre D.kern b then
178	            if IssueStatic (releaseEff D.kern b) st.entry (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra))
179	                x.dst then
180	              if InPlace st x extra then
181	                if SplitPre k (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
182	                    [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)] then
183	                  if StorePre (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
184	                      [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length
185	                      x.dst then
186	                    .ok ⟨storeEff (splitEff (releaseEff D.kern b) st.internal
187	                        [cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)]) (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length x.dst,
188	                      D.stacks.set j (growMeta st x extra (releaseEff D.kern b).A.length),
189	                      D.fresh⟩
190	                  else .reject
191	                else .reject
192	              else .fail
193	            else .reject
194	          else .reject
195	        else .reject
196	
197	/-- The state reached by the operations `os` from `D` when every step is `ok` (§58; DS-v1);
198	`none` as soon as a step is not `ok`. -/
199	def drun (D : DState) : List DOp → Option DState
200	  | [] => some D
201	  | o :: os =>
202	    match dstep k D o with
203	    | .ok D' => drun D' os
204	    | _ => none
205	
206	/-- The state reached by `os` from `DState.init statics` (§47; DS-v1); `DState.init statics` when a
207	step is not `ok` (used only under `(drun …).isSome = true`, see `druns`). -/
208	def dfinal (statics : Statics) (os : List DOp) : DState :=
209	  (drun k (DState.init statics) os).getD (DState.init statics)
210	
211	/-- A run of `os` from `DState.init statics` (§47; DS-v1) has only `ok` steps and reaches `D`; `D`
212	is library-reachable (`DReach`) and its kernel state is reachable (§57). -/
213	structure DRunsTo (statics : Statics) (os : List DOp) (D : DState) : Prop where
214	  /-- Every step of the run is `ok` and the run ends in `D`. -/
215	  run : drun k (DState.init statics) os = some D
216	  /-- `D` is reachable by library steps (DS-v1). -/
217	  dreach : DReach k statics D
218	  /-- The kernel state of `D` is reachable from `S3.init statics` by O1–O16 (§36, §57). -/
219	  reach : Reachable k statics D.kern
220	
221	/-- The run of `os` from `DState.init statics` has only `ok` steps (§47, §57; DS-v1). -/
222	abbrev DRuns (statics : Statics) (os : List DOp) : Prop :=
223	  DRunsTo k statics os (dfinal k statics os)
224	
225	end Exec

228	
229	/-- An `ok` outcome of the relation of a stack-library operation is a library step (DS-v1;
230	§57): a kernel step O1–O16 with the stack metadata unchanged, or a stack operation. -/
231	theorem dopRel_ok {k : K} {D D' : DState} : ∀ {o : DOp}, DOpRel k D o (.ok D') → DStep k D D'
232	  | .kernel o _, h => by
233	    obtain ⟨h, e1, e2⟩ := h
234	    have hD : D' = ⟨D'.kern, D.stacks, D.fresh⟩ := by rw [← e1, ← e2]
235	    rw [hD]
236	    refine .kernel ?_
237	    cases o with
238	    | derive => exact .derive h
239	    | split => exact .split h
240	    | release => exact .release h
241	    | transfer => exact .transfer h
242	    | depend => exact .depend h
243	    | enter => exact .enter h
244	    | exit => exact .exit h
245	    | read => exact .read h
246	    | write => exact .write h
247	    | writeShared => exact .writeShared h
248	    | pin => exact .pin h
249	    | unpin => exact .unpin h
250	    | endUse => exact .endUse h
251	    | free => exact .free h
252	    | alloc => exact .alloc h
253	    | store => exact .store h
254	    | newArena => exact h.elim
255	    | issue => exact h.elim
256	    | reset => exact h.elim
257	  | .newStack .., h => .newStack h
258	  | .push .., h => .push h
259	  | .mark .., h => .mark h
260	  | .rewind .., h => .rewind h
261	  | .grow .., h => .grow h

263	section Sound
264	variable {k : K} [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
265	  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
266	  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
267	
268	/-- A kernel outcome of the corpus runner, read on stack-library states, is an outcome of the
269	kernel relation with the stack metadata unchanged (§58; DS-v1). -/
270	theorem liftK_sound {R : Outcome3 S3 → Prop} {D : DState} {out : Outcome3 LState}
271	    (h : KRel R [] out) : KRelD R D (liftK D out) := by
272	  cases out with
273	  | ok L => exact ⟨h.1, rfl, rfl⟩
274	  | reject => exact h
275	  | fail => exact h
276	
277	/-- **Step soundness** (§58, §60–§75; DS-v1): the computed outcome of `o` from `D` is an outcome
278	of the relation of `o`, `ok`, `reject` and `fail` alike. -/
279	theorem dstep_sound (D : DState) (o : DOp) : DOpRel k D o (dstep k D o) := by
280	  cases o with
281	  | kernel o h =>
282	    have hs := lstep_sound (k := k) ⟨D.kern, []⟩ o
283	    cases o <;> first | exact liftK_sound hs | simp [kernelOp] at h
284	  | newStack st i =>
285	    show NewStackStep [] st i D _
286	    dsimp only [dstep]
287	    split
288	    · next h => exact .ok h
289	    · next h => exact .reject h
290	  | mark j =>
291	    show MarkStep j D _
292	    dsimp only [dstep]
293	    split
294	    · next h => exact .noStack h
295	    · next st h => exact .ok h
296	  | push j size dst =>
297	    show PushStep k j size dst D _
298	    dsimp only [dstep]
299	    split
300	    · next h => exact .noStack h
301	    · next st h =>
302	      split
303	      · next h1 =>
304	        split
305	        · next h2 =>
306	          split
307	          · next h3 =>
308	            split
309	            · next h4 => exact .ok h h1 h2 (.ok h3) (.ok h4)
310	            · next h4 => exact .store h h1 h2 (.ok h3) (.reject h4)
311	          · next h3 => exact .split h h1 h2 (.reject h3)
312	        · next h2 => exact .fail h h1 h2
313	      · next h1 => exact .static h h1
314	  | rewind j m =>
315	    show RewindStep k j m D _
316	    dsimp only [dstep]
317	    split
318	    · next h => exact .noStack h
319	    · next st h =>
320	      split
321	      · next h1 =>
322	        split
323	        · next h2 =>
324	          split
325	          · next h3 =>
326	            split
327	            · next h4 => exact .ok h h1 h2 (.ok h3) (.ok h4)
328	            · next h4 => exact .release h h1 h2 (.ok h3) (.reject h4)
329	          · next h3 => exact .split h h1 h2 (.reject h3)
330	        · next h2 => exact .static h h1 h2
331	      · next h1 => exact .dead h h1
332	  | grow j b extra =>
333	    show GrowStep k j b extra D _
334	    dsimp only [dstep]
335	    split
336	    · next h => exact .noStack h
337	    · next st h =>
338	      split
339	      · next hb => exact .noBlock h hb
340	      · next x hb =>
341	        split
342	        · next h0 =>
343	          split
344	          · next h1 =>
345	            split
346	            · next h2 =>
347	              split
348	              · next h3 =>
349	                split
350	                · next h4 =>
351	                  split
352	                  · next h5 => exact .ok h hb h0 (.ok h1) h2 h3 (.ok h4) (.ok h5)
353	                  · next h5 => exact .store h hb h0 (.ok h1) h2 h3 (.ok h4) (.reject h5)
354	                · next h4 => exact .split h hb h0 (.ok h1) h2 h3 (.reject h4)
355	              · next h3 => exact .fail h hb h0 (.ok h1) h2 h3
356	            · next h2 => exact .static h hb h0 (.ok h1) h2
357	          · next h1 => exact .release h hb h0 (.reject h1)
358	        · next h0 => exact .noExtra h hb (by omega)
359	
360	/-- An `ok` computed step is a library step (DS-v1; §58). -/
361	theorem dstep_ok {D D' : DState} {o : DOp} (h : dstep k D o = .ok D') : DStep k D D' :=
362	  dopRel_ok (h ▸ dstep_sound D o)
363	
364	/-- A run whose steps are all `ok`, from a library-reachable state, ends in a library-reachable
365	state (DS-v1; §47). -/
366	theorem drun_reach {statics : Statics} :
367	    ∀ {D D' : DState} {os : List DOp}, DReach k statics D → drun k D os = some D' →
368	      DReach k statics D'
369	  | _, _, [], hD, h => by cases h; exact hD
370	  | D, _, o :: os, hD, h => by
371	    unfold drun at h
372	    cases hs : dstep k D o with
373	    | ok D₁ => rw [hs] at h; exact drun_reach (.step hD (dstep_ok hs)) h
374	    | reject => rw [hs] at h; cases h
375	    | fail => rw [hs] at h; cases h
376	
377	/-- **Run soundness** (§47, §57; DS-v1): when every step of `os` from `DState.init statics` is
378	`ok`, the run reaches `dfinal k statics os`, which is library-reachable and whose kernel state is
379	reachable by O1–O16 (`DReach.reachable`). -/
380	theorem druns {statics : Statics} {os : List DOp}
381	    (h : (drun k (DState.init statics) os).isSome = true) : DRuns k statics os := by
382	  have hr : drun k (DState.init statics) os = some (dfinal k statics os) := by
383	    unfold dfinal
384	    cases e : drun k (DState.init statics) os with
385	    | none => rw [e] at h; cases h
386	    | some D => rfl
387	  have hd := drun_reach .init hr
388	  exact ⟨hr, hd, hd.reachable⟩
389	
390	/-- A computed `reject` is a `reject` outcome of the relation (§58; DS-v1). -/
391	theorem drejects {D : DState} {o : DOp} (h : verdictOf (dstep k D o) = .reject) :
392	    DOpRel k D o .reject := by
393	  have hs := dstep_sound (k := k) D o
394	  revert hs h
395	  cases dstep k D o with
396	  | ok => intro h; cases h
397	  | reject => intro _ hs; exact hs
398	  | fail => intro h; cases h
399	
400	/-- A computed `fail` is a `fail` outcome of the relation (§58; DS-v1). -/
401	theorem dfails {D : DState} {o : DOp} (h : verdictOf (dstep k D o) = .fail) :
402	    DOpRel k D o .fail := by
403	  have hs := dstep_sound (k := k) D o
404	  revert hs h
405	  cases dstep k D o with
406	  | ok => intro h; cases h
407	  | reject => intro h; cases h
408	  | fail => intro _ hs; exact hs
409	
410	end Sound

415	abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

417	/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
418	abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

423	/-- One stack (DS-v1, §72, §60, §65, §76 read for a stack): frame 1 with the stack value 0, the
424	storage 1 with the cells 2, 3, 4, and the destinations 5, 6, 7 (root authorities 0 on 0, 1 on 1,
425	2 on 5, 3 on 6, 4 on 7); `internal` 5, `Modify` derived from the root of the storage on its cells,
426	stored into the stack value; stack 0 created on 1 with `internal` 5. -/
427	def setup1 : List DOp :=
428	  [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, pt 1, pt 1, pt 1, lf, lf, lf]),

433	/-- Run of DS01 (DS-v1): mark `⟨0, 0, 0⟩`; `push` of 2 cells into 5 (block 6 on `[2, 3]`); mark

496	theorem DS03 : DRunsTo K0 [] ds03o ds03 ∧
497	    ds03.stacks = [⟨1, 5, [2, 3, 4], 3, [⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩], [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 2⟩]⟩] ∧

503	/-- **DS04** (DS-v1 "grow is in place only (…, extension into the space directly after the block,

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame

Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

/-- State reached by `ds03o` (§57; DS-v1). -/

/-- **DS03** (draft `case_grow`; DS-v1 "grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space
directly after the block, fail otherwise)"; class Lib). `grow(6, 1)` with one cell after the block;
then `grow(9, 1)` with no cell left; then `grow(6, 1)` of the replaced block. Expected (DS-v1):
`ok` (block `⟨0, 3, 9, 5⟩` of the same base and destination, authority 9 on `[2, 3, 4]`), `fail`;
for the replaced block, none from the source, to arbitrate: DS-v1 says nothing of a `b` that is no
block of the stack (the `reject` of the draft `case_grow` is module behaviour, not a source).
Obtained: `ok` (`release`, `split`, `store`, §62, §61, §65) with that block and footprint; `fail`
(no room, availability §77.4; readings DS-R5, DS-R6); `reject` (6 is no block of the stack;
reading DS-R5, whose recorded alternative, `fail` by analogy with DS-v1 "rewind m fails on a dead
or foreign mark", gives `fail` here: this conjunct is its example). Twin of the `fail` and of the
`reject`:
`grow(6, 1)` with one cell after the block, the `ok` step of this run. **MISMATCH** in form for the
    druns (by decide), by decide⟩

/-- Run of DS10 (DS-v1; §72): as DS09, but the callee receives only 11 (`Modify` on the stack value
0) and no right on the stack value 8; it marks stack 0 and pushes one cell of it into its local 13
(block 14). -/

  setup2 ++ [.push 0 1 5, .kernel (.derive 0 [0] .modify), .kernel (.enter [11] [lf, lf]),
    .mark 0, .push 0 1 13]

def ds10 : DState := dfinal K0 [] ds10o

`Modify` exercisable on the administering value", §77.1; DS-v1 "push and grow use the derived issue";
class Lib). The callee, without a right on the stack value 8, pushes two cells of stack 1 into its
local 14. Expected (§36, §77.1): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: `MetaRight` fails for stack 1, while
the callee has `Modify` on the destination 14. Twin: the same sequence with the parameter 12

inductive ResolveStep (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (m : Mode) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      ResolveStep j h m L .fail
  | noEntry {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ¬ DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ResolveRight L.kern pl m →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      DerivePre (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m →
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok { L with
        kern := deriveEff (compS L.kern pl m) L.kern.A.length (footprint L.kern.P sl.place) m
        res := L.res ++ [⟨pl.id, pl.internal, L.kern.A.length, m,
          [(L.kern.A.length + 1, h.slot, h.gen)]⟩] })
